how-much-does-kdp-take.html.text:
← KDP royalty calculator

How much does Amazon KDP take from author royalties?

KDP does not take one flat cut. An ebook's royalty depends on which of two plans it falls into by list price, and a paperback's royalty depends on a per-page print cost KDP deducts before you see a dollar. Neither is a single percentage a reader can quote from memory.

The 70% plan, and the delivery fee it carries

A list price from $2.99 to $9.99 qualifies for the 70% royalty plan. KDP pays 70% of the list price, then subtracts a delivery fee of $0.15 per MB of the file you uploaded.

LineAmount
List price$4.99
70% of list price$3.493
Delivery fee (2 MB x $0.15)-$0.30
Royalty per sale$3.193

The $2.99 cliff: the 35% plan is not a smaller slice of 70%

A list price under $2.99 does not get a reduced version of the 70% plan -- it drops onto the separate 35% plan entirely, and the delivery fee no longer applies. A $2.00 ebook nets just $2.00 x 0.35 = $0.70. Compare that to $3.193 on the $4.99 example above: pricing $2.99 lower does not cost 42% of the royalty, it costs 78% of it, because the plan itself changed underneath the price.

LineAmount
List price$2.00
Plan35% (below $2.99 floor)
35% of list price$0.70
Delivery fee$0.00 (35% plan has none)
Royalty per sale$0.70

Paperback: a per-page print cost comes out first

Paperback royalty is list price times a royalty rate (60% for sales on Amazon.com) minus KDP's own print cost -- a fixed charge plus a per-page charge that scales with the book, not a flat fee.

LineAmount
List price$14.99
60% of list price$8.994
Print cost ($0.85 + 280pg x $0.012)-$4.210
Royalty per copy$4.784

A color-interior book uses a higher fixed charge and per-page rate than black-and-white, and Amazon's own printing terms can change either constant -- verify against a current KDP print-cost report before pricing a new title.

Do this with your own numbers

The KDP royalty calculator runs this same arithmetic on your own list price, file size, page count, and sales volume, and compares staying KDP-exclusive against going wide to other stores and Ingram over the same 90-day window. Nothing you type leaves your browser.

Common questions

How much royalty does KDP pay on a $4.99 ebook?

On the 70% royalty plan (list price $2.99-$9.99), KDP pays 70% of the list price minus a delivery fee based on file size -- $0.15 per MB. A $4.99 ebook with a 2 MB file nets $4.99 x 0.7 - 2 x $0.15 = $3.193 per sale.

Why does a $2.00 ebook pay so much less than a $4.99 one?

It is not a smaller slice of the same 70% rate -- it is a different plan entirely. The 70% plan only applies to list prices from $2.99 to $9.99. A $2.00 ebook falls below that floor and is automatically paid on the 35% plan instead, with no delivery fee deducted: $2.00 x 0.35 = $0.70. That is less than a quarter of what the same book would net at $4.99 on the 70% plan ($3.193), for a book that costs only $2.99 less.

How much does KDP take on a paperback?

Paperback royalty is list price times a royalty rate (60% for Amazon.com sales) minus KDP's own print cost, which is a fixed charge plus a per-page charge. A $14.99, 280-page black-and-white paperback has a print cost of $0.85 + 280 x $0.012 = $4.21, so the royalty is $14.99 x 0.6 - $4.21 = $4.784 per copy.

index.html.text:
FOR SELF-PUBLISHED AUTHORS · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What does this book keep exclusive versus wide?

Put one 90-day window through Kindle Direct Publishing paid sales, Kindle Unlimited page reads, a KDP paperback, and the same book sold on other stores plus Ingram. The page reports the two totals. It does not tell you to enroll or leave KDP Select.

How much does KDP take from author royalties? · Should I enroll this book in Kindle Unlimited? · This calculator vs. Amazon's KDP royalty calculator · This calculator vs. a spreadsheet

Also emailing your readers directly? See the newsletter sponsorship rate calculator for pricing a sponsored placement to the same list.

Your book and your rates

70% / 35%, the $2.99–$9.99 70% band, delivery per MB, and 60% paperback minus print are starting points from Amazon's published KDP royalty help, not a live schedule. Overwrite every box from your current KDP royalty report and print preview. KENP rate changes monthly; paste this month's figure from your dashboard.

90-day readout

eBook net per paid sale
KDP paperback print cost
KDP paperback net per sale
KU page-reads needed to match one paid sale
Exclusive total
Wide total
KU page-reads that would match the wide extras

Exclusive is paid KDP ebooks + KU + KDP paperbacks. Wide is the same paid KDP ebooks and KDP paperbacks, plus other-store ebooks and Ingram paperbacks, and no KU. The two paths share the KDP paid-sale count on purpose: the decision this page prices is the KU window versus the wide extras, not a forecast of how visibility changes.

Already have your KDP royalty report? The KDP royalty report analyzer reads it and shows royalty, refunds and Kindle Unlimited pages per title — nothing uploaded.

Common questions

How many Kindle Unlimited page reads equal one paid sale?

On the starting example — a $4.99 ebook on the 70% plan with a 2 MB file and $0.15/MB delivery — one paid sale nets $3.193. At a $0.0045 KENP rate that is 709.6 Kindle Edition Normalized Pages. Your own list price, file size, plan, and this month's KENP rate change that number; the readout updates as you type.

Does this tell me to enroll in KDP Select?

No. It reports two 90-day totals on the numbers you typed. Enrolling, leaving, or staying in KDP Select is a contract decision you make against Amazon's current terms, not a recommendation this page can make.

Why can the paperback line go negative?

KDP paperback royalty is a share of list minus printing cost. A short book on a low list can have a print cost larger than that share. The page shows the negative rather than hiding it, because that is the arithmetic Amazon's own print preview is warning you about.

Is the print-cost formula the same as KDP's live preview?

No. The blank-override starting formula is a published-shape approximation (a small fixed amount plus a per-page rate, B&W or color) so the page has a number before you paste one. KDP's own print preview, for your trim, paper, ink, and marketplace, is the figure to paste into the override box.

What is left out?

Expanded distribution, hardcover, audiobook, VAT, currency conversion, ads, returns, and any change in paid-sale volume from being in or out of KU. Those are real, and they are not in this arithmetic. A later line can add them; inventing them here would be a forecast wearing a calculator's clothes.

should-i-enroll-this-book-in-kindle-unli.text:
← KDP royalty calculator

Should I enroll this book in Kindle Unlimited?

A $4.99 ebook is on the 70% plan. The file is 2 MB and delivery is entered at $0.15/MB. You expect 80 paid ebook sales in 90 days, 12,000 Kindle Unlimited page reads at $0.0045, a $14.99 paperback of 280 black-and-white pages with 20 KDP sales, and — if you stay wide — 40 other-store ebook sales at $2.50 net plus 10 Ingram paperbacks at a 40% wholesale discount and $5 print. These are starting points, not live Amazon figures. Overwrite them on the calculator.

Exclusive keeps $405.12. Wide keeps $491.06. Wide is ahead by $85.94 on this window. One paid ebook sale nets $3.193, which at $0.0045/page is 709.6 KENP. Matching the $139.94 of wide extras would take 31,097.8 KENP, more than the 12,000 in the example.

Change the KENP rate, the KU reads, or the wide volume and the ranking can flip. Forty thousand KU reads on the same book leaves exclusive ahead. The page still does not tell you to enroll.

Common questions

Should I enroll this book in Kindle Unlimited?

On the worked example — $4.99 ebook on the 70% plan, 2 MB file, $0.15/MB delivery, 80 paid ebook sales, 12,000 KU page reads at $0.0045, $14.99 paperback with 280 black-and-white pages, 20 KDP paperback sales, 40 other-store ebook sales at $2.50 net, and 10 Ingram paperbacks at a 40% wholesale discount and $5 print — exclusive keeps $405.12 and wide keeps $491.06. Wide is ahead by $85.94. That is arithmetic on those starting numbers, not a recommendation to enroll or leave.

How many KU page reads equal one paid sale on this example?

One paid sale nets $3.193. At $0.0045 per KENP page that is 709.6 pages. A 250-page book that is read all the way through is not automatically 250 KENP; KENP is Amazon's own normalized count from the file you uploaded.

How many KU page reads would match the wide extras?

The wide extras on this example are $100 of other-store ebook net plus $39.94 of Ingram paperback net, $139.94. At $0.0045 per page that is 31,097.8 KENP. The starting 12,000 reads do not reach it. Type a different KENP rate or a different wide volume on the calculator and the target moves.

vs-a-spreadsheet.html.text:
← KDP royalty calculator

This calculator vs. a spreadsheet

A royalty-tracking spreadsheet can total ebook, paperback, and Kindle Unlimited income correctly if every cell is filled in. What it usually charges instead of the real numbers is a flat 70% for every ebook sale and a rounded print-cost guess for every paperback -- and both shortcuts overstate the exclusive path the same direction, so a spreadsheet's own totals can quietly favor staying exclusive over a wide-distribution window that actually pays more.

What a royalty spreadsheet tracks, and what it rounds off

A royalty-tracking spreadsheetThis calculator
Ebook 70% royaltyList price × 0.7, most of the timeList price × 0.7 minus the delivery fee (file size × per-MB rate), every time
Paperback print costOne rounded number, reused for every titleA fixed charge plus a per-page rate, computed from this book's own page count and ink
KU page-read incomeA cell most authors already trackReads × the per-page KENP rate, same formula
Exclusive vs. wide, same 90-day windowTwo totals someone builds by handComputed from the same inputs on both sides, so nothing gets added to one side by mistake

Two rounding habits, one direction

Take this calculator's own default title: a $4.99 ebook (2 MB, 70% plan, 80 paid sales), a $14.99, 280-page black-and-white paperback (20 sales), 12,000 KU page reads, plus 40 other-store ebook sales and 10 Ingram paperbacks for the wide side of the comparison.

The ebook side. A flat 70% reports $3.4930 per sale. KDP actually pays list price × 0.7 minus the file's delivery fee (2 MB × $0.15/MB), which is $3.1930 -- thirty cents less, on every one of the 80 sales:

Flat 70% (no delivery fee)$3.4930/sale × 80 = $279.44
This calculator (70% minus delivery)$3.1930/sale × 80 = $255.44
Overstated by$24.00

The paperback side. A rounded "about $2 to print" guess is common shorthand. This 280-page book's real KDP print cost is a $0.85 fixed charge plus $0.012 a page -- $4.21, more than double the guess -- so the $2 shortcut overstates every paperback's royalty by $2.21:

Rounded $2.00 print-cost guess$6.9940/copy × 20 = $139.88
This calculator ($0.85 + $0.012 × 280 pages = $4.21)$4.7840/copy × 20 = $95.68
Overstated by$44.20

Neither shortcut touches the wide-distribution total at all -- both only inflate the exclusive side. Added together they overstate the 90-day exclusive total by $68.20, on a real gap of $85.94 in wide distribution's favor:

This calculator: exclusive$405.12
This calculator: wide$491.06 — wins by $85.94
Spreadsheet with both shortcuts: exclusive$473.32
Spreadsheet's apparent gapwide wins by only $17.74 — 79% of the real margin quietly erased

The book did not change. Two rounding habits that each look harmless on their own closed most of the distance between "wide clearly wins" and "close enough to keep guessing" -- on a title where the real numbers say the decision is not close at all.

Open the KDP royalty calculator to run this on your own numbers, read should I enroll this book in Kindle Unlimited? for the KU-page-reads walkthrough, or see this calculator vs. Amazon's own KDP royalty calculator if you want KDP's live print preview for one format instead.

Common questions

Why isn't the 70% royalty plan just 70% of list price?

KDP's 70% plan subtracts a delivery fee based on the ebook's file size before paying the royalty -- a flat 15 cents per megabyte in most marketplaces. A spreadsheet that multiplies list price by 0.7 and stops there skips that subtraction every time, so it overstates every single ebook sale by the same fixed amount.

Why does a rounded print-cost guess matter for paperback royalty?

KDP's print cost is a fixed charge plus a per-page rate, so it scales with page count rather than holding still. A spreadsheet that budgets a single rounded number -- picked once and reused for every title -- misses that scaling, and on a longer book the gap between the guess and the real formula can run several dollars a copy.

Do both shortcuts push the exclusive-versus-wide decision the same way?

Yes, and that is what makes them easy to miss: both quietly overstate what the exclusive-plus-KU path pays, which makes staying exclusive look better than it is relative to going wide. Neither shortcut touches the wide-distribution side of the comparison at all, so the two totals get pulled toward the wrong conclusion in the same direction rather than in ways that might cancel out.

Does this calculator store or upload anything I type?

No. Every field runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.

vs-amazon-kdp-royalty-calculator.html.text:
← KDP royalty calculator

This calculator vs. Amazon's KDP royalty calculator

Kindle Direct Publishing publishes a royalty help page and, inside a signed-in KDP account, a royalty calculator that prices printing cost and royalty for a list price, page count, ink, and marketplace. That is the right place to check what KDP would pay on one format you have already chosen.

Between that official preview and the decision still open — enroll this title in KDP Select for a 90-day exclusive window, or keep it wide — sits arithmetic the official tool does not do: how many Kindle Unlimited page reads match one paid sale, and whether this month's KU window still beats the other-store and Ingram volume you would keep by staying wide. This calculator does not try to reproduce KDP's live print cost. Paste the preview figure into the override box.

QuestionWhere to answer it
What will KDP pay on this list price, page count, ink, and marketplace? Amazon's own KDP royalty calculator, inside a KDP account.
What print cost does this exact trim and paper actually have? KDP's print preview on that title. Paste it into this page's override box.
How many KU page reads equal one paid sale? This calculator's 90-day readout — walked on Should I enroll this book in Kindle Unlimited?.
Does this 90-day exclusive window beat staying wide? This calculator's exclusive-versus-wide totals, on numbers you type.

Common questions

Should I use this calculator or Amazon's KDP royalty calculator?

Both, for different jobs. Amazon's KDP royalty calculator, published inside a KDP account, computes printing cost and royalty for a list price, page count, ink, and marketplace you already chose. It is the right place to check what KDP would pay on that one format. It does not compare Kindle Unlimited page reads to a paid sale, and it does not put a 90-day exclusive window next to the same book sold wide. This page does not try to replace KDP's live print preview — paste that figure into the override box — and instead answers the follow-on decision the official calculator leaves open.

Does Amazon's calculator require an account?

Yes. Amazon documents the royalty calculator as part of Kindle Direct Publishing, used from a signed-in KDP account on a title you are publishing or have published. This page is a static file. It needs no Amazon account and never talks to Amazon.
